summary: This note is a brief biography of Jack Clay, a theatre educator who studied speech at Northwestern University under Alvina Krause. It lists his teaching posts at Oberlin College, the University of Miami, and the University of South Florida, and his leadership of professional actor training programs at Southern Methodist University and the University of Washington. It also notes that he founded the professional acting company Stage #1 in Dallas and led it as artistic director for eight years.
one_line: Biography of Jack Clay, a theatre educator who taught at several universities and founded the Dallas acting company Stage #1.
key_facts: Jack Clay graduated from the Northwestern University school of speech under Alvina Krause.
Jack Clay taught at Oberlin College from 1956 to 1957.
Jack Clay taught at the University of Miami from 1957 to 1961.
Jack Clay taught at the University of South Florida from 1961 to 1966.
Jack Clay headed the Professional Actors Training Programs at Southern Methodist University from 1966 to 1986.
Jack Clay headed the Professional Actors Training Programs at the University of Washington from 1986 to 1991.
While in Dallas, Jack Clay founded Stage #1, a professional acting company.
Jack Clay served as artistic director of Stage #1 for eight years.
